answer.diagnosis: The structured layer-1 units fall into two groups. Large-blob detectors (0, 1, 8, 18, 19, 20, 22, 29) have a positive ring at radius about 5-6 with a negative centre. Small-blob detectors (14, 15, 23, 27) have a positive centre, a negative ring and high bias. In the background, which carries no size information, these units also show large weights (60-99, against a background level of about 20-35) at the same few isolated pixels, with signs consistent across units. Pixels whose brightness pushes toward 'small': (1,16), (1,17), (3,5), (3,12), (3,16), (4,16), (7,0), (8,0), (8,2), (9,0), (16,21), (17,20), (19,2), (19,12), (19,16), (20,19), (21,4). Pixels whose brightness pushes toward 'large': (23,11), (0,4), (0,11), (0,15), (0,17), (0,19), (23,4), (23,14). With i.i.d. background noise no single background pixel should carry label information. A fixed sparse dot pattern that differs by class is the likely explanation; this is an inference from the weights only. Layers 2-3 combine these detector groups with the matching signs, so the dots feed the logit directly. Fix: in each of the 12 structured units, replace every weight outside the blob region (rows 0-4, rows 19-23, and columns 0-3 and 20-23 of rows 5-18) with that unit's approximate mean background weight. This removes pixel-specific background cues but keeps the overall background-level response and the centre/ring size detectors unchanged. The means are rough estimates read from the grids.
